items.title: Nancy Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: John B. Williams... was with me for ten years before that... So when Arsenio was out on the road with us it was Michael Wolff, John B. Williams and Roy.

ctx.x: Great. That’s what you’re going to do tonight. Tell us about your current trio. I know Roy’s been with you.

Roy [McCurdy]. Oh forever. Roy and I obviously we ran into, I know Roy from the Cannonball Adderley days. But he’s been on the road with me for sixteen years. John B. Williams, who nationally is known on the Arsenio show for five years, but he was with me for ten years before that, and Arsenio, because I’m kind of Mom to him, said, “Mom can I really” —

items.title: Nancy Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: you did a 1981 trio album called At My Best with Mike Wolff, John B. Williams, and Roy McCurdy.

ctx.x: Let’s give their names. We’re talking about . . .

John B. Williams on bass, Roy McCurdy on drums. • Lou Llew Matthews, we’re getting up there in time, 18 years or so. He’s my conductor, and he has produced and arranged a lot of the things I’ve done for MCG – Manchester Craftsmen’s Guild. I got that part right. Ronnell Bright, I remember well. I can’t remember too many. The guys have been with me for so long that for me to try to remember who was with me 40 years ago is . . .
Yeah. The main ones were Don Trenner, Ronnell, and Mike Wolff.
